transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me today?

I can’t get past the feeling that I failed my brother. I’ve worked as an electrician for years, and if I couldn’t keep him safe, then I start thinking I’m a danger to anyone who works with me—or even anyone living in my house.
Can you tell me what happened to your brother?
I... I’m not sure I can talk about what happened yet. I just keep coming back to the feeling that I should’ve kept him safe.
Since this happened with your brother, have you been having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about it that intrude on your mind even when you don't want them to?
Yeah. I’ll be wiring a panel, or hear my nephew shut the garage door, and all of a sudden I’m back there—smelling smoke and seeing my brother. It feels like the job site just drops out from under me.
How long ago did this incident with your brother happen?
About four months ago. Ever since the garage fire, and my nephew came to live with us.
Since the fire, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, activities, or conversations—like electrical panels, garages, or talking about your brother—because they remind you of what happened?

Yeah. I don’t go into my own garage unless I absolutely have to. I quit helping with the electrical work at church, too. And if somebody starts talking about car projects or the fire, I shut it down pretty fast.
Since the fire, have you noticed feeling unusually jumpy, on edge, or easily startled—even in situations that aren't obviously dangerous?
I’m not really sure what you mean by jumpy. I mean, I’ve had a lot on my mind since then, but I don’t know if I’d call it that.
Aside from the moments when something reminds you of the fire, have you been feeling down, sad, or empty most of the day, nearly every day, over the past few weeks?
I wouldn’t say empty exactly. It’s more like this heavy guilt and anger sitting in my chest all day. Especially when I look at my nephew and think he lost his dad, and now he’s stuck with me instead.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with family?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about whether I enjoy things less.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed trouble concentrating or focusing on tasks, even ones unrelated to the fire or your brother?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether my focus is any different.
Since the fire, have you noticed yourself feeling constantly on guard or watchful, like scanning your surroundings for danger, even in safe places?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself scanning around or feeling on guard all the time.
Since the fire, have you felt distant or cut off from people close to you, even those you care about, like your nephew or other family members?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed feeling more distant from people close to me.
Since the fire, have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable or having angry outbursts, even over small things, more than before?
Yeah. Little things set me off now. An apprentice asks me the same question twice, or my nephew leaves tools out, and I’m yelling and cussing before I can stop myself.
Since the fire, have you had any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep at night?

Yeah. Most nights I’m lying there listening for crackling, or for a car door in the driveway. And when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up soaked from dreams about the garage. After that I usually can’t get back to sleep before work.
